evidence.excerpt: Three-layer films with an oriented polypropylene (OPP) structural layer, an adhesive tie layer, and an mLLDPE seal layer were produced by lamination. Seal-layer thickness was varied at 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 µm while total film gauge was held at 60 µm. Sealing experiments were conducted on a laboratory gradient heat-sealer over a 85–140 °C jaw temperature range; dwell time was fixed at 0.4 s and jaw pressure at 0.25 N/mm². Seal strength and hot-tack force were measured. Films with 20 µm seal layers achieved plateau seal strength of 31 N/25 mm and maintained hot-tack force above 6 N/25 mm over a 28 °C window (108–136 °C). Reducing the seal layer to 10 µm narrowed the hot-tack window to 16 °C and lowered plateau seal strength to 22 N/25 mm; increasing to 30 µm provided no significant benefit. Optical microscopy of cross-sections confirmed nominal thicknesses within ±1.5 µm. The 20 µm seal layer is proposed as the practical optimum for this film construction.
